name: Question 5
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-3x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-9x(t)+3y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector corresponding to the only eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ of the system's matrix $A$ is $v=[1,\text{ }3]^{T}.$ The vector $w={[-\frac{1}{3},\text{ }0]}^{T}$ is such that $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$  Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the system?

*Hint: Here, the dotted line represents the equilibrium solutions.*
worked_solution:
Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $v,$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

In our case, 

$$
\lambda =0,\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

 
Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t-\frac{1}{3} \\ 3t\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that ${x}_{E}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ are equilibrium solutions of the system since ${x}_{E}^{′}(t)=0.$ These solutions form the line with the equation $y=3x$ in the phase space, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14076166/assets/3a70188cf5de7e7b64530aa661447b7fa7fc1e918ca3de41088e67274d813b7a.png)

Now, we consider some general solutions of the form 

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t-\frac{1}{3} \\ 3t\end{aligned}].
$$

For example:

- When ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=3,$ we get the following curve: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3t \\ y=9t+3\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14076166/assets/37deb5a0fda7ef15a016ec2d73a3b935074b6696184dd480ebe5b858ce517500.png)

- When ${c}_{1}=-1$ and ${c}_{2}=-3,$ we get the following curve: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3t \\ y=-9t-3\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14076166/assets/60b49680cf94888122f25432586a3546dea206ae960f951afd187444afc8881a.png)

The phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14076166/assets/7b4de40b147f1745986476ab0b0cbad22ad0484924f62389c6c19187d5d06245.png)
